short_title: Simple Epithelium — Squamous, Cuboidal, Columnar & Pseudostratified

segments.script: A single layer of cells — yet four completely different types. Simple epithelium is where one layer does everything from gas exchange to immune filtration.
segments.video_prompt: A row of four simple epithelium types appears side-by-side from left to right as the narrator speaks: flat squamous tiles, cube-shaped cuboidal, tall columnar (with cilia on top), and mixed-height pseudostratified. Each glows in sequence as it is mentioned. Clean lab-report diagram style, white background, colour-coded cells.

segments.script: Simple squamous cells are flat, tile-like. Endothelium lines capillaries and the heart; mesothelium lines body cavities. Simple cuboidal has equal height and width — non-ciliated in kidney and thyroid; ciliated in respiratory bronchioles; brush-bordered in the PCT. Simple columnar is taller than wide — non-ciliated in stomach and gut; ciliated in fallopian tube and neurocoel; brush-bordered in intestinal mucosa. Pseudostratified — all cells touch the basement membrane but nuclei are staggered — traps particles in the trachea and bronchi.
segments.video_prompt: Step-by-step anatomical build-up. Each epithelium type appears as a cross-section panel in sequence. For each type: show cell shape (colour-coded), nucleus position (labelled dot), and a small organ location icon (lung alveolus, kidney tubule, fallopian tube, trachea). Pseudostratified has an arrow showing 'All cells touch BM' with staggered nucleus dots. Clinical white-background diagram style.
